reviewer_notes: I recomputed all arithmetic by hand. Every total in the 25 ideals is correct, including the five flagged rows: C005 (2,999 x 18 = 53,982 + 999 = 54,981; saving 6,981), C007 (48,000 - 10,000 = 38,000 best case), C012 (71,000 - 65,000 = 6,000; within 72,000), C021 (3 x (36,500 + 3,000) = 1,18,500; 3 x (38,000 + 3,000) = 1,23,000) and C025 (880 x 1.13 = 994.40; 920 x 1.13 = 1,039.60). The flags are false positives from multi-step arithmetic. The decisions are sound and no ideal invents a fact. The problems are structural. (1) Every row uses the same template: 2 options, 1 review each, and an option that is clearly worse; no row is a NO-MATCH and no row has 3+ options. (2) There is no n in any review ('R1: owner reports'), so calibration can't be graded. (3) 9 rows cite reviews as bare 'R1 describes...' with no brackets (C007, C008, C010, C012, C014, C019, C020, C022, C023), and C019 has no bracketed citation at all, so a code citation check can't see them. (4) Three Hinglish queries get English replies (C001, C022, C023), but only C001 was flagged by code. (5) There are 3 non-India rows (C015 UK, C020 US, C025 Canada) against a cap of 1. (6) Coverage against the spec is thin: there are only 3 used or refurbished rows (C003, C004, C023), and none gives an F6 checklist or says that condition can't be judged from photos. There is 1 team row (C021), with no GST and no ambiguity between per-unit and total budget. There are no F5 tables, no card or exchange stacking, no te-en or ta-en rows, and no service rows tied to a city. (7) Product names are reused across scenarios (Forge15 in C002 is also in A001 and A026), and suffixes like 'Plain15-P16' are invented. (8) Some user facts sit only in the evidence and not in the query ('Budget ₹36,000', 'User prioritizes avoiding repair disruption'), so the model is graded on facts the user never typed. All 116 S5 assertions are typed semantic. About 40 are exact totals or budget checks that code could grade.

rows.proposed_ideal: I can't promise seven years for either laptop; no review here covers that long, so the ₹80,000 stretch you made conditional on a promise doesn't apply. On durability evidence, Long-L16 is the stronger option: one writer used it for two years with one battery replacement [R1], its memory is upgradeable, and its warranty is three years. Thin-T16 has only six trouble-free months behind it [R2] and a one-year warranty. What is your budget without the stretch? If ₹74,000 fits it, I'd lean Long-L16; if only ₹69,000 does, Thin-T16 is the option, with less evidence and a shorter warranty. Before paying, check that spare parts and battery replacements are sold for Long-L16.
assertion_issues: Add (critical): 'Does not treat ₹80,000 as available once the promise is refused'
